outcome: Deviations from normal pregnancies and births (prolonged labour, caesarean sections, induction of labour, vacuum extraction, bleeding)
Exaggerated pregnancy problems (great nausea, pelvic pain)
Lack of understanding in the healthcare system
Perceived abuse of power in healthcare
Need for control and participation in decision-making in childbearing
Need for protecting children from potential violence
cohort: The study included nine female childhood sexual abuse (CSA) survivors who participated in 16 in-depth interviews.
finding: The study found that childhood sexual abuse (CSA) survivors experienced widespread poor physical and mental health, complicated childbearing processes including negative birth experiences, and significant difficulties in their interactions with healthcare professionals due to a perceived lack of understanding.
mod_finding: Many participants experienced deviations from normal pregnancies and births, including prolonged labour, caesarean sections, induction of labour, and vacuum extraction, with nearly all reporting a negative birth experience.
